newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada consumer holiday spending seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Canada consumer holiday spending seen higher.

text.p: Canadian retailers can hope for some joy this holiday season after a survey this week showed consumers are likely to open their wallets a little wider than last year.
"People always underestimate how much they'll spend," said Brent Houlden, a partner in the retail group at accounting firm Deloitte & Touche. "I was surprised as to how buoyant it was."

The nationwide Gallup poll, conducted in early September for Deloitte & Touche, found 49.5 percent of Canadians would spend the same amount this holiday season as last year, while 23.5 percent said they would spend more and 21.6 percent less.
Last year's dismal retail results over the Christmas season reflected political concerns and a sluggish economy.
Despite consumer optimism, "it's still not going to be a great Christmas this year," Houlden said.

The recent bankruptcy of showroom catalogue retailer Consumers Distributing, with 216 stores across Canada, will depress the profits of other retailers as its stock is sold off at discount prices between now and year-end, he added.
"That will steal Christmas from the other retailers," Houlden cautioned,

The Gallup survey broke down responses by income, occupation and mother tongue. Consumers with lower incomes tend to anticipate more holiday season spending this year as a treat to themselves, while higher income earners like to splurge year-round, Houlden said.

The survey found differences between native French and English speakers. About 59.3 percent of respondents whose mother tongue is French expected to spend the same amount this year, compared with 48.1 percent of English speakers.

Another 20 percent of native French-speakers said they would spend more, while 15.2 percent expected lower expenditures, the survey showed. This compared with 22.5 percent of English-speakers who said they would increase spending, while 24.2 percent saw less expenditure.
"There's definitely an opportunity here for retailers to tailor their advertising," said Houlden.
Gallup surveyed 1,231 Canadians. The survey is considered accurate within 2.9 percent.
